'''Demetrius Jackson Jr.''' (born September 7, 1994) is an American college basketball player who recently completed his college career for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|University of Notre Dame]]. Born in [[South Bend, Indiana]], he played high school basketball for [[Marian High School (Mishawaka, Indiana)|Marian High]].

==High school career==
Jackson played high school basketball for [[Marian High School (Mishawaka, Indiana)|Marian High School]].<ref name="undbio">{{cite web|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/demetrius_jackson_851625.html|publisher=University of Notre Dame|title=Demetrius Jackson Bio|accessdate=April 9, 2015}}</ref> As a junior he averaged 22.3 [[points per game]], 6.6 rebounds per game, 4.4 assists per game and 2.0 steals per game, led his school to sectional championship and was named to the All-State Underclass First Team.<ref name="undbio"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ibcacoaches.com/resources/boys_all-state_underclass_teams.aspx|publisher=Indiana Basketball Coaches Association|title=Boys All-State Underclass Teams|accessdate=April 9, 2015}}</ref> As a senior Jackson averaged 25.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.6 steals per game, finishing as runner-up for the [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] to [[Zak Irvin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.inkfreenews.com/2013/04/03/marians-jackson-2nd-in-mr-basketball/|publisher=Inkfreenews.com|title=Marian’s Jackson 2nd In Mr. Basketball|accessdate=April 10, 2015}}</ref> He concluded his career at Marian as the all-time leading scorer in St. Joseph County with 1,934 career points.<ref name="si">{{cite web|url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/03/04/demetrius-jackson-notre-dame-fighting-irish-acc|title=Demetrius Jackson's journey from foster care to Fighting Irish star|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=March 4, 2015|accessdate=April 7, 2015}}</ref> His performances with Marian earned him a selection for the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], and he was the first [[Northern Indiana]] native to receive this honor since [[Shawn Kemp]] in 1988.<ref name="si"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/021513aaa.html|title= Demetrius Jackson Selected To Play In 36th Annual McDonald's All-American Game|publisher=Notre Dame Athletics|date=February 15, 2013|accessdate=April 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.southbendtribune.com/2013-04-03/news/38257553_1_demetrius-jackson-chris-thomas-fast-break|title=Jackson competes with country's best|publisher=South Bend Tribune|language=|date=April 3, 2013|accessdate=April 7, 2015}}</ref> Jackson finished the game with 5 points, 4 assists and 2 steals and won the Jack Daly Sportmanship Award and the Skills Competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.southbendtribune.com/2013-04-04/news/38287280_1_demetrius-jackson-all-american-game-mcdonald|title=Jackson plays pass-first game at McDonald's showcase|publisher=South Bend Tribune|date=April 4, 2013|accessdate=April 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mcdonaldsallamerican.com/content/aag/en/MediaCenter/background-materials/All-time-stats/_jcr_content/featuredcontent/everything/file.res/All%20Time%20Stats%20and%20Award%20Winners%20-%202015.pdf|title=McDonald's All American Games All-time Stats and Award Winners|publisher=Mcdonaldsallamerican.com|date=December 19, 2014|accessdate=April 7, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==

===Freshman season===
Jackson committed to play for [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], under coach [[Mike Brey]] instead.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/recruiting/eye-on-college-basketball-recruiting/20386347/star-point-guard-demetrius-jackson-pledges-to-notre-dame|title=Star point guard Demetrius Jackson pledges to Notre Dame|publisher=CBSsports.com|date=September 27, 2012|accessdate=April 8, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/09/27/report-2013-point-guard-demetrius-jackson-staying-home-to-play-at-notre-dame/|title=2013 point guard Demetrius Jackson staying ‘home’ to play at Notre Dame|publisher=NBCsports.com|date=September 27, 2012|accessdate=April 8, 2015}}</ref> In his [[2013–14 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|freshman]] season Jackson was expected to back up guards [[Eric Atkins]] and [[Jerian Grant]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thesportsbank.net/college-bball/15-notre-dame-fighting-irish-basketball-437/|title=#15 Notre Dame Fighting Irish: College Basketball 111 in 111|publisher=Thesportsbank.net|date=October 30, 2013|accessdate=April 8, 2015}}</ref> Jackson commented on the situation, saying that although he had been apprehensive to play along a [[Senior (education)|senior]] point guard, he realized that it would benefit his game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8432855/demetrius-jackson-chooses-notre-dame-fighting-irish-illinois-fighting-illini|title=Notre Dame lands Demetrius Jackson|publisher=ESPN|date=September 28, 2012|accessdate=April 8, 2015}}</ref> 
He scored in double digits for the first time versus [[2013-14 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team|Santa Clara]], tallying 13 points.<ref name="undbio"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ndinsider.com/basketball/mens/notre-dame-men-s-basketball-going-small-boosts-irish/article_99b70bc3-a55c-593d-9262-6330701568d2.html?mode=jqm|title=Notre Dame men's basketball: Going small boosts Irish|publisher=ndinsider.com|date=November 22, 2013|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref> In February, he missed two games in order to deal with academic issues.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wndu.com/home/headlines/Demetrius-Jackson-returns-to-Irish-practice-after-6-day-academic-leave-245882741.html|title=Demetrius Jackson returns to Irish practice after 6-day academic leave|publisher=wndu.com|date=February 17, 2014|accessdate=April 8, 2015}}</ref> Upon returning to the team he scored a season-high 17 points against [[2013–14 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]].<ref name="undbio"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.onefootdown.com/2014/2/19/5428352/miami-hurricanes-outlast-notre-dame-basketball-71-64|title=Miami Hurricanes Outlast Notre Dame Basketball 71-64|publisher=Onefootdown.com|date=February 19, 2014|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref> He concluded the season having started half of his 30 games and averaging 6.0 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.<ref name="undbio"/><ref name="espnprofile">{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/66284/demetrius-jackson|title=Demetrius Jackson Player Profile|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
In his [[2014–15 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|sophomore season]] Jackson scored a career-high 22 points against [[2014–15 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]], in the first meeting between the schools in 35 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cnsnews.com/news/article/notre-dame-edges-no-19-michigan-state-79-78-ot|title=Notre Dame edges No. 19 Michigan State 79-78 in OT|publisher=CNSNews.com|date=December 4, 2014|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref> A couple of weeks later he tied this mark against [[2014–15 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/12/20/connaughton-no-21-notre-dame-beat-purdue-94-63/20710009/|title=Connaughton, No. 21 Notre Dame beat Purdue 94-63|publisher=USAToday.com|date=December 20, 2015|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref> Jackson produced solid performances for the Irish in the [[2015 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2015 ACC Tournament]] against [[2014–15 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]], [[2014–15 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] and [[2014–15 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and he was eventually named to the All-ACC Tournament second team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/66284/demetrius-jackson|title=Demetrius Jackson 2014-15 Game Log|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://ndsmcobserver.com/2015/03/notre-dame-storms-north-carolina-win-acc-championship-game/|title=Notre Dame storms by North Carolina to win ACC Championship Game|publisher=ndsmcobserver.com|date=March 17, 2015|accessdate=April 10, 2015}}</ref> He helped his team proceed to the Elite 8 of the 2015 NCAA Tournament by scoring 20 points against [[2014–15 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/notre-dame-races-wichita-state-81-70-ncaa-tournament-article-1.2163984|title=Notre Dame races by Wichita State 81-70 in NCAA Tournament|publisher=nydailynews.com|date=March 27, 2015|accessdate=April 13, 2015}}</ref> Throughout the season he averaged 12.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.6 steals per game appearing in all 38 games of his team.<ref name="espnprofile"/> On April 14, 2015 it was reported by ESPN that Jackson would return to the Fighting Irish squad for his [[2015–16 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|junior season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12687652/point-guard-demetrius-jackson-returning-notre-dame-junior-season|title=Guard Demetrius Jackson to return to Notre Dame for junior season|publisher=ESPN|date=April 14, 2015|accessdate=April 14, 2015}}</ref>

===Junior season===
On February 1, 2016, he was named one of 10 finalists for the Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Nortlander|first1=Matt|title=Cat Barber, Fred VanVleet missing from list of Cousy Award finalists|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25468790/cat-barber-fred-vanvleet-conspicuously-missing-from-cousy-award-finalists|accessdate=February 2, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|accessdate=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>

At the conclusion of his junior season, Jackson announced his intention to forgo his final season of eligibility and enter the [[2016 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite url|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/sports/ci_29701845/college-basketball-notre-dames-demetrius-jackson-kansas-wayne|title=College basketball: Notre Dame's Demetrius Jackson, Kansas' Wayne Selden Jr. to enter NBA draft|author=AP Staff|work=mercurynews.com |date=30 March 2016 |accessdate=30 March 2016}}</ref> He is projected to be taken somewhere in the Top 20.

==Personal==
Jackson, a [[South Bend, Indiana|South Bend]] native, is the son of Demetrius Jackson Sr. and Juanita Jones.<ref name="si"/> Jackson lived in two different foster homes after the age of twelve, before finally settling with the Whitfields, the family of then basketball teammate Michael Whitfield.<ref name="si"/><ref>{{cite web|publisher=Scholastic, University of Notre Dame's Student Magazine|url=http://scholastic.nd.edu/issues/54692-demetrius-jackson-the-transformation/|title=Column: The Transformation of Demetrius Jackson|date=December 14, 2014|accessdate=April 9, 2015}}</ref> As a student in the [[University of Notre Dame]], he enrolled in the College of Arts and Letters.<ref name="undbio"/>
